title: India and China hold Corps Commander talks on Arunachal Pradesh
summary: A second round of Corps Commander-level talks on the eastern sector ended after about ten days, aimed at reducing friction before winter.
body: India and China have concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks focused on tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh. The talks began on 8 November and ran for about ten days with a break. The Indian side was led by the General Officer Commanding of III Corps, with a Ministry of External Affairs official present.

Reports describe the talks as cordial. The aims were to set rules of engagement, reduce friction between troops, keep communication channels open and lower tensions before winter, when both sides keep large deployments in the area.

In August 2026, Special Representatives talks produced an eight-point set of outcomes on border management, including two new military hotlines and two additional meeting points for commanders. Analysts describe the present phase as controlled stabilisation of the LAC rather than a final settlement.
India's stated position is that unilateral attempts to change the status quo on the LAC are unacceptable.

- The LAC is divided into western (Ladakh), middle (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand) and eastern (Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh) sectors.
- The McMahon Line is India's position on the boundary in the eastern sector.
- India's border with China is about 3,488 km long.
